claims.text: Evidence in analysis is the exact words from the text that show the feature a point is about; without it a point is only assertion.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Selecting evidence means taking the shortest stretch of words that carries the feature: three words that do the work beat three lines that surround it.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A quotation is the text’s own words; a paraphrase is the writer’s retelling. As evidence for a feature only a quotation will do, because the feature lives in the exact words.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Interpreting a quoted word means saying what it means in this place and what it suggests beyond that; both parts are needed, because a word can carry a literal sense and an attitude at once.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: An analytical point with no words from the text to support it cannot be checked by a reader, so it carries no weight; a detail misread, and built on, sinks the answer.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: An embedded quotation is a short quotation worked into the grammar of your own sentence, so the analysis and its evidence arrive together.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: To embed a quotation: choose a short phrase, fit it into your sentence’s grammar so it reads as part of your sentence, and comment on the words inside it.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Short quotations work because every word quoted can then be analysed; a quoted sentence is mostly padding, and only two or three of its words were ever doing the work.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A line reference is a location, not evidence: it tells a reader where to look but does not show the choice, so it substitutes a map reference for the thing itself.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Quoting whole sentences, or citing a range of lines, instead of the words that matter leaves a reader hunting for the feature and pads the answer with text it must re-read.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Analytical verbs join evidence to effect precisely: suggests, conveys, evokes, positions, undercuts each say something different about how the choice works on the reader.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A stock phrase is one that could follow any quotation anywhere ("this engages the reader"); a precise statement of effect could have been written for these words only, and names what this reader is led to think, feel or do.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The reader a precise effect statement names is the text’s own audience — the worried resident, the browsing shopper — not a generic "reader" who exists nowhere.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Following a quotation with a stock effect phrase, one that could follow any quotation, analyses nothing: the words quoted and the effect named must match each other and only each other.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: An analytical paragraph has four parts: a claim about the text, the evidence that shows it, the analysis of what the evidence does, and the link to the text’s purpose.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Building an analytical paragraph in four moves: state the claim, quote the few words that show it, analyse what those words do to this reader, then say how that effect serves what the text is for.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A coherent line of argument across a whole analysis is a single view of the text that each paragraph advances from a different side, joined by links that carry the reader from one to the next.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: An argument about a text organises its observations as evidence for a view; a list of observations sets them side by side and lets them add up, or not, by accident.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A string of separate observations with nothing joining them into a view of the text leaves the reader to do the analysis, and reads as though the writer stopped at the collecting stage.

verification.method: Authored originally for the YYeni 9093 AS build under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).
